title: ClientWSProtocol
description: Browser <-> control-plane WS protocol (§6.2). These 4 shapes are independent named payloads, not a discriminated union, so (per the PR-05 spec) there is deliberately no top-level oneOf here — each is emitted as its own top-level $def. Connect -> subscribe{token, clientId} within 30s (timeout lives in a later PR's platform/timeouts.go) -> a single 'subscribed' reply (SubscribedPayload: full state + event replay + artifacts + participants) -> broadcast stream. fetch_history is cursor-paginated. Close codes 4001 (re-auth) / 4002 (token expired) are connection-level, not part of these payload shapes. Field nullability convention: 'nullable' means a required key whose value may be JSON null.

SubscribeRequest.description: Sent by the browser client immediately after connecting; must arrive within 30s (§6.2).

token.description: Per-participant WS token minted via REST (/api/sessions/:id/ws-token).

SubscribedPayload.description: The single reply to subscribe. state/events/artifacts/participants are deliberately loosely typed here (additionalProperties: true) — the full session/turn/sandbox read-model shape is assembled by later PRs; this schema only fixes the top-level envelope.

state.description: Full session/turn/sandbox read model (shape assembled by later PRs).

eventsTruncated.description: True when events is a cut prefix of this session's full history rather than all of it -- the fixed item-count cap or the byte-size budget was hit. False means events is the session's complete history to date. A client that needs what was cut already has fetch_history.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor; null to start from the beginning/most recent (server-defined).

limit.description: Null means use the server default page size.

nextCursor.description: Null when there are no more pages.
